title: DX Playbook Waves: SDKs, Docs, and Quickstarts Initiative
creator: Maya Johnson
description: Goal: Consolidate and operationalize a repeatable set of ‘Playbook Waves’ that bundle SDK examples, authored docs, and 5–7 minute quickstarts targeted at specific developer personas (platform engineers, frontend, and ML engineers). The intent is to drive measurable first-success moments, reduce time-to-integration from hours to <2 hours, and create an OKR-linked cadence for continuous improvement. Scope: 1) Template SDK starter kits (Node/Python/Go) with opinionated defaults and metrics hooks; 2) Doc modules per persona covering authentication, best practices for batching/caching, and rollout patterns; 3) Two canonical quickstarts (sample app + guided tutorial) per wave; 4) Telemetry and checkpoints for funnel metrics (activation, first-call success, retention). Out of scope for this wave: deep localization, legacy SDK refactors, and full enterprise onboarding flows. Success metrics: activation rate (first successful API call) +15% within 30 days of wave launch, median time-to-first-success <= 90 minutes for sample cohort, NPS for onboarding docs >= 4.0 (external survey). Deliverables: playbook checklist, starter SDK repos with CI tests, three authored doc modules, two quickstart tutorials, dashboards for funnel signals, and a retro + follow-up backlog.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK starter repos pass CI and have a runnable sample; 2) Docs published under /docs/dx/playbooks with a feedback widget; 3) Quickstarts tested by 3 internal beta users and updated; 4) Activation funnel dashboards show event instrumentation; 5) Launch checklist signed off by PM, Eng lead, and Documentation owner.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: prioritize minimal friction over feature-complete SDK surface in wave 1 (no advanced streaming examples).
Consider 'opinionated defaults' to reduce cognitive load; include config presets for batching and cache TTLs.
We will reuse existing auth snippets from the onboarding repo to avoid duplication.
